concepts.def: Northwest and west: older, harder rocks (granite, slate); higher relief; e.g. Scottish Highlands, Lake District, Snowdonia.
Southeast: younger, softer sedimentary rocks (chalk, clay); flatter relief; e.g. London Basin, East Anglia.
Diagonal line dividing UK between upland west/north and lowland south/east; reflects geological boundary.
Last Ice Age (until c.10,000 years ago) shaped uplands with U-shaped valleys, corries, ribbon lakes.
UK's 17,820km coast includes rocky (Cornwall), chalk (Dover), sandy (East Anglia), estuarine (Severn).
Major rivers (Thames, Severn, Trent) flow from uplands to lowlands; demonstrate upper, middle, lower course features.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Physical Landscapes in the UK — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Physical Landscapes in the UK brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Physical Landscapes in the UK.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which line divides upland and lowland Britain?
options: Watford Line
Tees-Exe Line
Hadrian's Wall
Severn-Trent Line

mcqs.q: Where are softer sedimentary rocks found in UK?
options: Scottish Highlands
Southeast England
Snowdonia
Lake District

mcqs.q: Why does deforestation increase flood risk?
options: Stratified sampling means picking samples from different strata of rock.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
Trees intercept rainfall, their roots increase infiltration and transpiration removes water — removing them increases surface runoff and reduces lag time, peaking river levels faster.
Deforestation causes floods because trees normally hold water in their branches forever.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between random, stratified and systematic sampling?
options: Stratified sampling means picking samples from different strata of rock.

Random: every member has equal chance of selection. Systematic: pick every nth item. Stratified: divide the population into groups and sample proportionally from each — ensures subgroup representation.
All three sampling methods produce the same results.
Deforestation has no effect on rivers — only rainfall matters.
